title: Install rtkit so PipeWire gets realtime priority
author: zacksiri
body:
Fixes #9390

## Summary

Omarchy ships the full PipeWire stack but not `rtkit`. PipeWire requests realtime scheduling from RealtimeKit over D-Bus at startup; with the service absent, every `mod.rt` request fails (`RTKit error: org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.ServiceUnknown`) and all data-loop threads run at `SCHED_OTHER` nice 0. The fallback paths are also absent on a stock install: no `LimitRTPRIO` in the shipped user units, no `realtime-privileges` group, empty `limits.d`. The result is audio xruns/crackling under sustained CPU/GPU load — invisible at idle, which is what makes it so hard to trace.

## Changes

- **`install/omarchy-other.packages`**: add `rtkit` next to the pipewire family — covers fresh installs
- **`migrations/1789747667.sh`**: repair existing installs — install `rtkit` via `omarchy-pkg-add` and restart the running audio units so PipeWire's priority request succeeds without a reboot. Idempotent, matching the established migration patterns (cf. the kernel-headers and KEF no-suspend migrations)

Fresh ISO installs mark all shipped migrations complete during finalize-user, so the two paths don't overlap.

## Verification

- Confirmed the failure mode on Omarchy 4.0.4, NVIDIA multi-GPU desktop: `pacman -Q rtkit` missing, journal full of `ServiceUnknown`, data threads at `SCHED_OTHER` — reported on #9390 with two further hardware confirmations there (Intel T2 MacBook, ThinkPad X1 Carbon)
- After installing `rtkit 0.14` alone and restarting `pipewire`/`wireplumber`: main PIDs get `nice -11`, data loops get RT scheduling, and crackling under full 3-GPU llama.cpp inference load is gone
- `bash -n` clean; migration follows the sourced-script conventions in `agents/skills/migrations.md`

files.patch:
@@ -36,6 +36,7 @@ pipewire-alsa
 pipewire-jack
 pipewire-pulse
 qt6-wayland
+rtkit
 snapper
 sof-firmware
 thermald

@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+echo "Install rtkit so PipeWire gets realtime priority"
+
+# PipeWire requests realtime scheduling via RealtimeKit at startup, but rtkit
+# is not a dependency of Arch's pipewire packages and the rlimits fallback is
+# not configured either (see https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/9390).
+# Without it, audio threads run at SCHED_OTHER nice 0 and produce xruns under
+# sustained load.
+omarchy-pkg-add rtkit
+
+# rtkit only takes effect when PipeWire re-requests priority at startup.
+# Restart the audio units if they are running; harmless when idle or as root.
+systemctl --user try-restart pipewire.service pipewire-pulse.service wireplumber.service 2>/dev/null || true

comments.body:
Relationship to #7971: that PR takes a different mechanism (realtime-privileges package + `realtime` group + pam_limits so processes can self-elevate via `RLIMIT_RTPRIO`, also covering Hyprland's own RT request), while this one is the minimal audio-only fix via rtkit, directly targeting #9390. PipeWire's `module-rt` tries rtkit first and falls back to `RLIMIT_RTPRIO`, so the two are compatible rather than competing — rtkit would win for PipeWire if both landed, and #7971 would still add value for the compositor. Neither blocks the other.

One packaging note in case it comes up: #7971's body states a package listed only in `omarchy-other.packages` "never reaches a machine". That's no longer true for the current repo — `docs/file-layout.md` says both `omarchy-base.packages` and `omarchy-other.packages` are ISO pacstrap lists, and `pipewire-alsa`/`pipewire-jack`/`pipewire-pulse` ship exclusively in `omarchy-other.packages` while being installed explicitly on every stock system. `rtkit` is therefore placed alongside the pipewire family it supports. Happy to move it if maintainers prefer it in `omarchy-base.packages`.

This also fixes something worse than xruns, see #12443. Without rtkit, xdg-desktop-portal's Realtime interface reports `RTTimeUSecMax=0`, and module-rt in every PipeWire *client* applies that as a hard `RLIMIT_RTTIME` of 0 to its own process. quickshell is such a client and is also the launcher, so everything started from the menu inherits the zero and gets SIGKILLed by the kernel the moment it has a real-time thread. On linux-omarchy that kills SteamVR's compositor at startup.

One thing I measured that matters for the migration: installing rtkit was not enough on a running session.

```
$ pacman -S rtkit
$ busctl --user get-property org.freedesktop.portal.Desktop /org/freedesktop/portal/desktop org.freedesktop.portal.Realtime RTTimeUSecMax
x 0                                    # still 0, new PipeWire clients still get RLIMIT_RTTIME 0/0
$ systemctl --user restart xdg-desktop-portal
x 200000                               # new PipeWire clients now get 200000/200000
```

So the migration probably wants `xdg-desktop-portal.service` in its `try-restart` list too. Processes that already carry the hard zero keep it, since a hard limit can't be raised: the shell, and so every menu launch, stays affected until `omarchy-restart-shell` or the next login.
